intent.subject: Shalabi leads the silent marsh file after the radio blackout.
intent.action: He taps the dead radio, signals silence across his lips, then raises his compass and points a new bearing as the file quietly swings behind him.
intent.setting: Moonlit Tina Plain marsh, with shallow water and darkness surrounding the advancing company.

research.claim: The company is shown beginning its march through the Tina Plain/marsh after the early helicopter drop.
research.note: Follows production decision D-1 to use the Egyptian account of the early Tina Plain drop and long march; the landing location and march distance remain disputed and require the episode end-card source note.

research.claim: The precise setting of this first-march moment as full night is not explicitly established in the ledger.
research.note: H-05 and H-08 support the drop and march, but do not establish this beat's exact time of night.

research.claim: Composite Corporal Mahmoud sends/receives and decodes the coded radio traffic, warns Shalabi that the signal was intercepted, worries about losing contact with command, and switches off the set.
research.note: Mahmoud is a composite character. His actions dramatize the sourced intercepted-signal and radio-silence event without assigning it to a documented real individual.

research.claim: Captain Hamdi Shalabi orders radio silence after the intercepted-signal warning.
research.note: The coded warning and Shalabi's radio-silence order are stated by the primary Egyptian account; the marked dialogue is a permitted dramatized paraphrase.

research.claim: Shalabi taps the switched-off radio and draws a finger across his lips to communicate the sourced radio-silence order; the file passes the silent signal back man to man.
research.note: Permitted staging under P-01: the gestures visually show the sourced radio-silence order and add no new event or outcome.

research.claim: Composite Sergeant Sayed hears the silence order and asks whether the enemy is waiting for them.
research.note: Sayed is a composite character; the question is fictional character dialogue and does not credit him with a documented act.

research.claim: Shalabi uses his compass, changes the file's bearing, and directs the company toward an unexpected approach after the interception warning.
research.note: The route-change dialogue is an approved paraphrase of the source treatment that the enemy did not expect anyone to come from that direction. The compass and turning-file business are permitted P-01 staging.

research.claim: The Soviet-pattern manpack radio, whip antenna, handset placement, and use of red light are presented as period equipment/detail.
research.note: The ledger documents radio traffic and silence, but does not source this specific radio model/configuration or red-light procedure.

flags.detail: The beat fixes the company's first steps into the marsh at night, but the ledger does not establish the exact time for this moment.
The specific Soviet-pattern manpack radio configuration, whip antenna, handset placement, and red-light decoding procedure are not sourced in the ledger.

direction.coverage: Open on the silent file in moonlit marsh, tighten to Shalabi’s dead radio and hush signal, then hold a medium-wide as compass-led turn ripples through the men.
direction.blocking: Shalabi halts at point, taps the radio, hushes the line, raises the compass, and pivots to a new bearing as the file silently arcs behind him through shallow water.
direction.performance_note: Play Shalabi as controlled and economical—urgency contained in his eyes and precise gestures, never panic.
direction.pacing: Measured, near-silent beats that accelerate subtly on the collective turn.
direction.tone_ref: Restrained historical war realism: cold moonlight, wet darkness, and disciplined fear under pressure.

crowd.note: A disciplined marsh column in mud-worn khaki, standing and moving through mid-shin brine; the silence hand sign passes back along the file before they quietly arc behind Shalabi onto the new bearing.

wardrobe.additions: Egyptian captain's rank: exactly three small gold five-pointed stars in a row on each plain khaki shoulder strap, plain khaki collar with no collar tabs or badges, compass on a lanyard (PRP-0008)
visible_details: Bare-headed short black hair, damp and flattened under cold moonlight.
Sand-khaki cotton field jacket with two buttoned chest-pocket flaps; sleeves rolled to the forearms.
Plain khaki collar with no tabs or badges; exactly three small gold five-pointed stars in a row on each plain khaki shoulder strap, catching only a restrained glint.
1970s Soviet-pattern khaki canvas chest rig with three closed-flap AK-magazine pouches, cotton straps and simple metal buckles; aluminium canteen in canvas cover on web belt.
Compass PRP-0008 on its lanyard, raised clearly in his hand as he indicates the new bearing.
Trousers are soaked dark with mud and brine above the knees; black leather combat boots disappear into mid-shin marsh water and mud.
Jacket hem, sleeves and chest rig show wet mud splashes, brine-darkened fabric and occasional water drips.
wardrobe.notes: WS priority: bare head, captain shoulder-star silhouette, raised compass and period canvas webbing must read. Continue WEAR_MUD: wet, darkened lower half rather than dried salt crust; no radio is assigned to Shalabi.

visible_details: Bare-headed Egyptian commando file, short dark hair visible; no helmets or modern headgear.
1970s sand-khaki cotton field uniforms with plain khaki collars, rolled sleeves, Soviet-pattern khaki canvas webbing and closed-flap pouches.
Dark mud-and-brine soaking rises from boots to above the knees, with wet splashes on trouser fronts and jacket hems; water level remains mostly mid-shin.
AKM rifles with fixed wooden stocks and other period anti-tank loads are held at chest height, on shoulders or above the water; nothing rests in the marsh.
The passed-back no-radio hand sign is readable among the nearest turning men; distant file reads as wet khaki silhouettes quietly pivoting behind C-01.
wardrobe.notes: At wide-shot scale, prioritize the disciplined bare-headed wet-khaki file, raised/secured period weapons, and the silent hand-sign relay. Do not make individual rank markings legible except C-01's captain stars.

makeup.skin_state: Medium-olive skin is cold-damp under moonlight, with a restrained sweat-and-brine sheen across his high forehead, hollow cheeks, thin nose, upper lip and exposed neck. Fine black marsh-mud flecks and narrow brine trails mark his jaw and cheeks; fatigue subtly darkens beneath his narrow eyes. No blood or visible wounds.
makeup.hair_state: Bare-headed short black hair retains its neat side part but is humidity-damp and flattened, with a few wet strands separated at the forehead. Thin handlebar mustache remains intact, damp, and lightly salt-flecked.
makeup.notes: Keep the face readable in cool moonlight; wet skin and hair match the mud-and-brine-soaked uniform state.

makeup.skin_state: Egyptian male faces and exposed hands are cold-damp with restrained sweat and brine sheen, scattered fine black mud flecks on cheeks, brows, jaws and necks, and subtle tired under-eye shadows. Lower trouser legs are mud-darkened above the knees; no blood, wounds, or gore.
makeup.hair_state: All are bare-headed with short black hair, humidity-damp and flattened; a few wet strands cling at hairlines. Keep any moustaches natural, intact, and lightly damp.
makeup.notes: The file reads as exhausted but disciplined, with wet marsh texture kept subdued in the blue-black moonlight.

dressing: Vast unbroken black mud flats with thin irregular white salt crust
Shallow mid-shin brine sheets and narrow reflective puddles between crust islands
Sparse low salt-marsh scrub, flattened and dark at the waterline
Small boot-disturbed mud ripples and broken salt plates marking the file's halted path
No horizon structures, roads, vehicles, flags, or additional personnel
set.set_state: Shalabi stands at the head of the halted column in mid-shin brine on a firmer salt-crust patch, tapping PRP-0007 held clear of the water before using PRP-0008 to indicate the new route as the men silently arc behind him.
set.notes: Keep the radio, compass, rifles, and all carried loads above the brine; cold moonlight catches wet salt crust and shallow reflections while the surrounding marsh falls into blue-black darkness.

camera.light: Cold moonlight and starlight from high camera-left/back skim the salt crust, shallow mid-shin brine, wet uniforms and raised weapons, leaving the far marsh blue-black; Shalabi’s face, radio tap, lips, compass and pointing hand receive only the same faint natural moon edge and soft sky return, with no artificial fill or visible practical.
camera.exposure_note: Hold the negative about 1.5 stops under a normal night exterior: preserve readable detail on Shalabi’s eyes and gesture sequence in the central band while retaining deep black-blue shadows, restrained water reflections and a nearly featureless horizon.
camera.framing_note: Generate 16:9 for a 2.39:1 crop; keep Shalabi, his radio, lips, raised compass and new-bearing hand within the middle 75% frame height, with the silent file’s turning hand-sign chain legible behind him in deep focus. Low 24mm camera stays near the brine surface without placing faces or key hands near crop edges.

action.choreography: Shalabi halts in mid-shin brine, makes the radio-silence signal clearly and economically, then leads the file into a quiet pivot onto the new bearing. The column’s turn travels rearward as a controlled ripple, with men keeping spacing and their steps low to avoid splashing.
action.movement: Slow, load-bearing turn through mud and shallow brine; boots lift minimally and settle deliberately, with water never above the knees.
beats: Shalabi stops at the head of the file and braces on firmer mud.
He taps the dead radio once without fumbling.
He draws one finger across his lips; the nearest men repeat the no-radio sign down the file.
He raises the lanyarded compass, checks it, and points the new bearing.
He pivots and advances; the column silently swings behind him.
action.safety_note: Use stable, tested mud footing and a slow pivot path; keep performers in mid-shin water and avoid forceful steps that create conspicuous splashes.

reasons: The intent identifies Shalabi (C-01), his post-blackout silence-and-reroute action, the Tina Plain marsh setting (LOC-0003), night, and an appropriately tense stealth mood.
It preserves the beat’s key dramatic action: enforcing radio silence and changing the company’s bearing.
The included references cover the named character and location; the signal/order itself requires no additional ID.
The direction includes all required elements: coverage, blocking, a performance note, pacing, and a tone reference.
Coverage clearly tracks the intended action from the silent file to the dead radio/hush signal and the compass-led change in direction, while preserving the group response in a medium-wide view.
Blocking accurately stages Shalabi at the head of the file, his radio tap and silence signal, the compass bearing, and the file’s quiet pivot through shallow marsh water.
The performance note supports a restrained, grounded command presence, with contained urgency rather than melodrama.
Measured near-silence, subtle acceleration during the turn, and the cold, wet historical-war realism are consistent with the stealthy, tense, urgently tactical night-marsh scene.
The commando crowd uses the correct production archetype, but its count is unspecified (`None`). The definition of done requires a count for every crowd entry.
revise_instructions: Assign an explicit, renderable number of `egyptian_commandos` for the visible column, sized to support a readable hand-sign relay and arcing turn in the wide frame.

reasons: The period uniform, bare-headed appearance, captain insignia, webbing, and lifted period weapons are correct. However, the wide-shot visible-details list promises inspection-level captain-star detail that a 24mm WS is not expected to show, contrary to the wide-shot detail requirement.
revise_instructions: Keep the captain's three-star shoulder insignia as required costume construction/continuity, but remove it from promised readable WS detail or qualify it as visible only if the shoulder happens to resolve in the frame. Retain the raised compass, bare head, muddy lower uniform, and period webbing as the primary wide-shot reads.

reasons: The commandos' makeup states that “mud and brine rise consistently to above the knees on their bodies.” This conflicts with the locked marsh rule: standing men are normally in mid-shin water and only reach knee depth in occasional pockets, never above the knee.
revise_instructions: Revise the commando makeup continuity so brine/wetness physically reaches mid-shin, with knee-level wetness only for isolated deeper-pocket men. Mud splashes or stains may extend higher from prior marching, but do not describe brine or waterline above the knees.

reasons: The shot requires Shalabi to tap a dead radio, and both camera and action explicitly frame/use that radio, but the set lists no radio in props, hand props, dressing, or set state. This also breaks continuity with the previously established dark PRP-0007 radio.
revise_instructions: Place PRP-0007 in the set as the same inert, fully dark environmental radio from the prior shot, braced low just above the mud where Shalabi can tap it without lifting it. It need not become a hand prop. Keep PRP-0008 as Shalabi's actively handled compass.
Remove the unsupported “folded topographic map” addition from the compass description unless it is separately cleared and placed as a period prop; the locked carried prop is the compass.

reasons: The choreography is concrete and respects the shallow-water rule, but it relies on a dead radio that Set does not place. Its weapon-handling field is also blank despite the moving armed column and the requirement for period-correct, plain weapon handling during physical action.
revise_instructions: After Set restores PRP-0007, retain the low, unlifted radio tap. Add a concise weapon-handling instruction: commandos keep fixed-stock AKMs and anti-tank loads slung at the chest, shoulder, or held clear of mud and brine throughout the halt and turn; no weapon manipulation or firing.

reasons: Locked C-01 casting is preserved, and the only additional visible group is supplied as a production commando crowd archetype with a defined count, wardrobe, wear state, and appropriate marsh-file behavior.
C-01 has the required 1973 captain insignia of exactly three gold five-pointed stars on each plain khaki shoulder strap, with no prohibited collar tabs or chest eagle badge.
Both Shalabi and the commando crowd are bare-headed, use period-correct khaki uniforms and Soviet-pattern canvas webbing, and keep weapons and anti-tank loads above the brine.
The mud and brine treatment respects the shallow-marsh rule: standing water is mid-shin, with only isolated knee-depth pockets.
Makeup covers both the lead and all visible commandos, maintains bare-headed short dark hair, restrained fatigue, brine dampness, and non-graphic mud wear appropriate to the night march.
C-01's stated signature features remain preserved and readable, with no injuries, blood, or gore.
The dead radio PRP-0007 is placed as an inert, dark environmental continuity prop at Shalabi's halt point, while locked carried prop PRP-0008 is correctly assigned as a hand prop.

The dressing establishes a period-plausible shallow salt marsh with mid-shin brine, mud, salt crust, halted footprints, and a new curved turning track; it introduces no modern equipment, text, or unsupported combat event.

The setup follows the locked WS, 24 mm, static, moonlit-night design and includes a valid low-exposure strategy that keeps the key face, hands, radio, compass, and signal relay readable without making night appear like daylight.
The crop-aware framing keeps the required action in the 2.39:1 center band while retaining shallow-water and horizon cues.
The action concretely delivers the required order of events: halt, tap the dark radio, silence gesture, compass bearing, directional point, hand-sign relay, and silent file turn.
Weapon handling remains period-correct and safely keeps rifles and loads clear of mud and water; movement explicitly stays below knee depth for standing men.

PRP-0007 is actively tapped by Shalabi in this shot, but it is listed only as environmental dressing/prop rather than a hand prop. The definition of done requires any prop an actor uses in the shot to be identified as a hand prop.
revise_instructions: Add PRP-0007 to hand_props as the fixed, mud-braced radio Shalabi physically taps, while retaining its placement low at the halt point, its inert dark state, and PRP-0008 as Shalabi's carried compass.

department_notes: camera: The director’s requested opening-to-tightening-to-medium-wide coverage cannot occur within this locked static wide shot; retain the complete radio-silence and route-change action in one wide composition.

wardrobe: The director's requested tightening and medium-wide hold conflict with the locked static WS/LENS_WIDE_24 shot; retain the locked wide framing, with Shalabi's compass and nearest hand-sign relay staged clearly enough to read.
makeup: The Director’s requested progression from wide to tight to medium-wide coverage conflicts with the locked static wide-shot camera design.
set: The Director's requested tightening coverage conflicts with the locked static wide-shot camera design; retain the locked WS/LENS_WIDE_24 framing.
action: The locked static wide shot conflicts with the Director’s requested opening, tightening, and medium-wide coverage progression; retain the static WS.
action: The specified radio interaction requires the otherwise optional, non-locked PRP-0007 to be present in Shalabi’s immediate reach.

critic: The Director's coverage instruction to open on the file, tighten to the radio/hush signal, then hold medium-wide conflicts with the locked static WS/LENS_WIDE_24 camera design. Camera correctly follows the lock.

critic: The locked Wave-2 manifest calls PRP-0007 an optional, non-locked beat prop that is mostly carried by off-screen characters, while the locked shot description and action require Shalabi to tap a dead radio. This prep elects to include PRP-0007 as Shalabi's hand prop; human clarification is needed on whether the radio is required for this shot despite its optional manifest status.
